ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High macro-level contrast characterized by a dominant central low-intensity black core transitioning to high-intensity white/light-blue lateral lobes, with an approximate 45:55 pixel distribution ratio.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Central region contains a large contiguous black geometric mass extending from the peduncle insertion to the median notch. Lateral lobes feature extensive black linear mottling and vertical streaking superimposed on a white background, with higher density of dark pixels near the leading edge.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Sharp V-shaped central depression with a calculated angle of approximately 72 degrees and a deep bounding-box penetration relative to the lobe width.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, high-amplitude serration map along the entire trailing boundary. Notable irregular peaks and valleys ranging from 3 to 12 pixels in depth, with increased jaggedness near the lateral terminals.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly concave trailing edge curve leading to acute, pointed lateral tips; the leading edge presents a slight convexity.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Highly localized clusters of roughly circular, high-contrast white and grey pixel formations consistent with barnacle colonization located at the extreme distal tips of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Numerous unaligned vertical and diagonal black linear disruptions (rake marks) clearly visible across the high-intensity white regions of both the left and right lobes.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A distinct irregular notch or loss of tissue on the trailing edge of the right lobe immediately adjacent to the median notch. Presence of significant protruding calcified masses on the rightmost terminal edge.
other_distinctive_markers: A singular, high-intensity white circular pixel cluster (potential focal scar or puncture) is visible in the upper quadrant of the right fluke lobe, isolated from the general mottling pattern.
